title: Understanding Why Large Language Models Can Be Ineffective in Time Series Analysis: The Impact of Modality Alignment

problem.claim: The study examines whether and why large language models are effective for core time series analysis tasks.

gap.claim: LLMs are not designed for time series tasks, and existing reprogramming techniques may not meaningfully align time series data with language-model representations.

contributions.claim: The authors conduct experiments comparing LLMs with simpler baselines and randomly initialized LLMs across forecasting, classification, imputation, and anomaly detection.
The authors analyze reprogramming techniques using data manifold analysis to assess modality alignment.
The authors release code for the experiments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LLMs provide minimal advantages and may distort temporal structure in the evaluated core time series tasks.
The authors report that simpler models consistently outperform LLMs while using far fewer parameters.
The authors report that existing reprogramming techniques exhibit pseudo-alignment behavior in embedding space.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have shown impressive apparent performance in time series analysis.
Simpler models can achieve comparable performance with substantially less complexity.
The study evaluates LLMs across four core time series tasks and compares them with simpler baselines and randomly initialized LLMs.
LLMs offer minimal advantages and may distort temporal structure, while simpler models consistently outperform them with fewer parameters.
Reprogramming techniques show pseudo-alignment, suggesting performance may arise from intrinsic time series structure rather than meaningful language-model alignment.

source_observation.claim: Simpler models consistently outperform LLMs in the reported core time series tasks while requiring fewer parameters.

interpretation.claim: Model complexity and language-model pretraining may not provide task-relevant benefits when the data structure can be captured by simpler models.

application.claim: Benchmark complex models against strong simple baselines before attributing gains to architectural sophistication.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson extends beyond the evaluated tasks, datasets, and models.

source_observation.claim: Existing reprogramming techniques exhibit pseudo-alignment rather than effective alignment between time series data and language representations.

interpretation.claim: Transfer mechanisms should be evaluated for representation-level alignment rather than assumed to transfer capabilities across modalities.

application.claim: Use embedding-space or manifold analyses when assessing whether a cross-modal adaptation mechanism creates meaningful alignment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which alignment analyses, datasets, or reprogramming methods were used.

unknowns: Datasets, metrics, model implementations, and exact experimental results are unspecified.
The magnitude and statistical reliability of the reported performance differences are unspecified.
The scope of the conclusions beyond the evaluated time series tasks is unspecified.
